title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: Removing unread Remote Config keys checked its offsets against the disk and turned them into positions through the buffer. One line added above and the deletion landed an entry lower.

highlights.title: Remote Config keys deleted at the right place
highlights.description: The offsets were checked against a fresh disk read, then converted through `openTextDocument`, which returns the buffer when the file is open and unsaved. Both now use the text the edit will land in, and a file that moved is left alone.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Removing unread Remote Config keys could delete the wrong entry when the file was open with unsaved changes. The fault is older than the dialog, which only widened the window.
The edit is rebuilt after the answer, like the other three bulk commands, so what is applied is what is reported.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: All four bulk commands now hold the same two rules: an offset is only valid against the text the edit will land in, and what is applied is what is reported.
